items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And one time they were going to do a tour with Benny Goodman and they were trying to get all the original guys that were still alive and — this is a true story — and Louis Armstrong’s band.

ctx.x: He could. What’s that, there’s some story I heard about Gubenko, him calling someone Gubenko.

Well he always called me Gubenko. He calls anybody Pops. Well I’ll tell you. Well I know maybe the story you’re talking about. He always called everybody Pops and he always called me Gubenko. He loved that name. Now we’re doing the Ed Sullivan Show. And this goes, naturally it’s much more of a story than just the Gubenko. We’re doing the Ed Sullivan Show and there was one show that Teddy Wilson couldn’t be on because he had other commitments. So they hired a piano player called Bernie Leighton. White guy.…

Benny’s about ready to walk to the right and he says, “Hey Benny.” Now Benny gets a little curve. He never heard that in rehearsal at all. Now walking off he threw a curve and Ed Sullivan was in left field himself, so you get two guys up there, and he says to Benny, “Benny, who’s in the band?” Because he had to ask to kill some time. And Benny looks over at the band and looks at me first, he tried to say Terry, he tried his best, “Uhh Gubenko.” My mother loved it, my relatives loved it, whoa, what a hit. But then…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: he was going to do a tour with Louis Armstrong and the Benny Goodman band

ctx.x: Excellent. When I got to about the middle of the book and I turned the page and I saw the title of the chapter Foggo, I said I know who he’s going to talk about now.

You know everybody has a Benny Goodman story but not everybody living — one of my most fun times is I used to do a lot of the jazz cruises, you know, 90 musicians would be on a cruise. And Mel Powell was on one of the cruises. And Mel Powell worked with Benny Goodman way before I did. And we sat there one night talking about Benny Goodman stories, and who else? Maybe Ken Peplowski, he worked for Benny Goodman. Whoever was there that knew Benny Goodman, and it was actually like a bunch of comedians sitting around…

of them, the agent, he told Joe Glaser, “Get me” this is in New York, “Get me Ziggy Elman.” Ziggy Elman was in California. So I go to the first rehearsal I went with Joe Glaser to Benny’s rehearsal, even though I wasn’t going to be on the show I just wanted to hear the band. And I’m standing with Joe Glaser and Benny looks at me and he says, “I asked you to get me Ziggy Elman on the trumpet” he says. “That’s Ziggy Elman, I flew him in” and Joe Glaser would use every F word in the world, you know I’m telling you,…
